title: Desire, Etc. for the Not-Self Exterior
html:
• Saṁyutta Nikāya 35.183–185 Linked Discourses 35.183–185
  • 17. Saṭṭhipeyyālavagga 17. Sixty Abbreviated Texts

Bāhirānattachandādisutta Desire, Etc. for the Not-Self Exterior

“Yo, bhikkhave, anattā, tatra vo chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. “Mendicants, you should give up desire … greed … desire and greed for what is not-self. Ko ca, bhikkhave, anattā? And what is not-self?

Rūpā, bhikkhave, anattā; tatra vo chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. Sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas are not-self …” Saddā … gandhā … rasā … phoṭṭhabbā … dhammā anattā; tatra vo chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. Yo, bhikkhave, anattā tatra vo chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti.
